writeup.headline: Alphabet rates Hold: strong growth, quality and net cash offset by high valuation and weak trend.
writeup.thesis: Alphabet scores 59, a Hold, 6 points short of the Buy band. Growth (74) is solid, with TTM revenue growth of 20.1%, latest-quarter revenue growth of 24.2% year on year, and growth sped up by 2.4 pp from the previous quarter. Quality (71) and the balance sheet (100) also support the score: the operating margin is 33.1% and the company holds net cash, with cash at 2.42 times debt. Valuation is the main drag at 24. In absolute terms the multiples are high (P/S 8.8x, P/FCF 74.1x, EV/EBIT 25.8x, FCF yield 3.6 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield), and the stock is expensive against its own history, with P/FCF more expensive than at 57 of the last 61 month-ends. A weak trend score (43), with the price 20.4% below its 52-week high and shares 16.9 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days, plus a middling news score (55) hold the rating back.
key_risks: Q3 operating income and EPS came in well below estimates despite strong revenue growth.
Heavy AI capex weighs on free cash flow: the FCF margin is 11.9% against a 33.1% operating margin.
High absolute valuation, with P/FCF at 74.1x, leaves little room for disappointment.
Search antitrust appeals and EU DMA compliance review remain unresolved.
Weak price trend: price 6.0% below its 200-day average and lagging SPY and QQQ.
what_would_change: A 6-point gain in the composite score would reach Buy, for example through a recovering price trend or better news flow on earnings and guidance.
Free cash flow growing faster than the share price would lower P/FCF and lift the valuation score from 24.
A drop of more than 15 points would mean Sell, which would likely take a growth slowdown together with weaker quality or worsening news such as adverse antitrust rulings.
Further Cloud and TPU momentum showing up in profits, not just revenue, would support growth and quality.
